title: Are You Secretly A Narcissist?
seoTitle: Are You Secretly A Narcissist? | Personality Quiz
seoDescription: Take a playful personality quiz about confidence, attention, empathy, feedback, validation, and self-image patterns.
summary: A light self-reflection quiz about confidence, attention, empathy, feedback, validation, and self-image patterns.

homepage.title: Are You Secretly A Narcissist?
homepage.summary: Answer quick questions about compliments, attention, feedback, and confidence to reveal your self-image pattern.
homepage.thumbnailAlt: Mirror and journal collage for a self-image personality quiz

landing.quickStartText: Choose what feels most honest. Your self-image pattern appears instantly at the end.

footer.aboutText: This quiz looks at everyday patterns around confidence, attention, compliments, feedback, self-image, empathy, and how easily you share space with others. Your result shows the personality-style pattern that appeared most often in your answers. This quiz is for entertainment and self-reflection only. It does not diagnose narcissism, narcissistic personality disorder, personality disorders, mental health conditions, abuse, or relationship safety.
footer.topicText: The word narcissist is used here in a casual, pop-culture way. In this quiz, it refers to everyday patterns around confidence, attention, feedback, self-image, and empathy. It is not a clinical label or professional assessment.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Reflective Balancer.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a self-aware pattern: you like feeling respected, but you also notice other people's needs and can step back when the situation needs it.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Confident Connector.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a warm confidence pattern: you enjoy being seen, but your best moments still include curiosity, humor, and genuine interest in others.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Validation Seeker.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a validation style that likes reassurance. A kind word, clear approval, or small sign of appreciation can matter more to you than you always admit.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Spotlight Striver.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to an attention pattern that enjoys recognition. You often feel most energized when your effort, personality, or talent gets noticed.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Image Curator.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a presentation pattern: you care about how things look, how your choices are understood, and whether people see you the way you intended.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Control Planner.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a planning pattern that prefers order, preparation, and predictable expectations. You relax more easily when the shape of the moment makes sense.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Sensitive Defender.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a feedback pattern that feels things strongly. Criticism, awkward moments, or being misunderstood can stay in your mind longer than you expected.

profiles.title: Your self-image pattern is The Boundary Builder.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a growth pattern around space and timing. You are building the skill of knowing when to jump in, when to pause, and when sharing attention makes the moment better for everyone.

stageGroups.title: First Impressions
stageGroups.encouragement: Your first instincts already reveal a pattern.

questions.prompt: What do you secretly want people to notice first?
choices: That you are thoughtful and easy to trust
That you seem comfortable with yourself
That you have something impressive about you
questions.explanation: First impressions often reveal the kind of recognition that feels most rewarding.

questions.prompt: When you meet someone new, what do you usually hope happens?
choices: You get a moment to show your personality
They seem to like you quickly
They remember something distinctive about you
questions.explanation: Your social hopes point toward how you prefer to be received.

questions.prompt: Which entrance feels most like you?
choices: Quietly joining and noticing the mood of the group
Making sure you look prepared and composed first
questions.explanation: The way you enter a space can show whether comfort, connection, or presentation leads.

questions.prompt: What makes you feel most comfortable in a group?
choices: Knowing everyone has room to speak
Knowing people are responding well to you
questions.explanation: Comfort often comes from the kind of social order you trust most.

questions.prompt: Which compliment would you remember longest?
choices: You always know what you are doing
questions.explanation: The compliment that lingers often matches your favorite version of yourself.

questions.prompt: When someone forms a quick opinion of you, what do you hope they get right?
questions.explanation: What you want understood first can reveal what feels most personal.

stageGroups.title: Compliments And Attention
stageGroups.encouragement: The way you receive attention can reveal a lot.

questions.prompt: Which compliment do you replay later?
questions.explanation: The praise you replay hints at the self-image you want to keep.

questions.prompt: What happens when praise feels a little vague?
choices: You accept it and move on
You wish they had been more specific
You quietly wonder how it sounded to everyone else
questions.explanation: Your response to vague praise shows how much detail you need to feel seen.

questions.prompt: What do you do when you are not getting attention?
choices: Check whether someone else needs the moment
Find a natural way to join back in
Start wondering why the energy shifted
questions.explanation: Low-attention moments can reveal how steady your self-image feels.

questions.prompt: When someone praises a friend in front of you, what is your first private reaction?
questions.explanation: Comparison can be quiet, quick, and revealing.

questions.prompt: Which kind of attention feels best?
choices: Warm appreciation from someone who knows you
A whole room noticing your effort
Respect for how prepared you were
questions.explanation: Different kinds of attention reward different parts of the self.

questions.prompt: How do you usually respond to a big compliment?
choices: Say thanks and keep it grounded
Enjoy it and add a little charm
Point out the details they may have missed
questions.explanation: How you receive praise can show whether steadiness, connection, or visibility leads.

stageGroups.title: Criticism And Feedback
stageGroups.encouragement: Feedback can show how you protect your self-image.

questions.prompt: What kind of criticism stays with you?
choices: When someone says you missed their feelings
When someone says you made the wrong impression
questions.explanation: The feedback that sticks often points to the part of your image you protect.

questions.prompt: When someone corrects you, what helps most?
choices: A chance to explain your thinking
questions.explanation: Your preferred repair style shows what makes feedback feel manageable.

questions.prompt: If you make a small mistake in public, what is your first instinct?
questions.explanation: Public mistakes can reveal how closely you track other people's reactions.

questions.prompt: Which feedback style works best for you?
questions.explanation: The delivery you prefer reveals the conditions where you can listen best.

questions.prompt: When you disagree with feedback, what do you usually do first?
choices: Feel the sting before you can think
questions.explanation: Your first move after feedback shows how quickly self-protection appears.

questions.prompt: What do you want people to understand after giving you feedback?
choices: That one comment is not the whole story
questions.explanation: The explanation you want to add often protects your preferred self-image.

stageGroups.title: Empathy And Listening
stageGroups.encouragement: This round looks at how attention can be shared.

questions.prompt: When a friend tells a long story, what do you do naturally?
choices: Listen for what they are really feeling
Connect it to something you have experienced
Wait for the part where you can help structure it
questions.explanation: Your listening style can show whether empathy, connection, or structure comes first.

questions.prompt: What makes a conversation feel satisfying?
choices: The energy feels fun and mutual
questions.explanation: A satisfying conversation tells us what kind of social win you value.

questions.prompt: When someone has a different preference than you, what is easiest?
choices: Explaining why your plan works better
questions.explanation: Preference differences show how naturally you make room for another view.

questions.prompt: What do you notice when someone goes quiet?
choices: You may have lost their attention
questions.explanation: Quiet moments can turn attention outward or back toward your own standing.

questions.prompt: How do you show you care in a conversation?
questions.explanation: Care can sound like curiosity, warmth, or confident direction.

questions.prompt: What is hardest during a conversation you did not choose?
choices: Not checking how you are coming across
Letting it unfold without guiding it
questions.explanation: Less exciting conversations reveal where attention naturally drifts.

stageGroups.title: Confidence And Comparison
stageGroups.encouragement: Confidence is tested when someone else gets attention.

questions.prompt: How do you react when someone outshines you?
choices: Feel motivated to raise your level
Wonder if people still noticed you
questions.explanation: Another person's strong moment can reveal how secure you feel.

questions.prompt: When do you feel most confident?
choices: When your choices match your values
When people are clearly enjoying your presence
When everything is going according to plan
questions.explanation: Confidence can come from values, attention, or structure.

questions.prompt: What makes you compare yourself to someone?
questions.explanation: The comparison that hooks you points toward what you value in yourself.

questions.prompt: Which private thought feels most familiar?
choices: I hope I handled that well
I hope they noticed my effort
I hope I did not look uncertain
questions.explanation: Private thoughts often reveal the standard you use to judge yourself.

questions.prompt: If someone is better than you at something, what helps?
choices: Practicing until you feel ahead again
questions.explanation: Your response to skill gaps shows how flexible your confidence is.

questions.prompt: What kind of success feels most satisfying?
choices: A result that proves your method worked
questions.explanation: Success can reward inner growth, visibility, or control.

stageGroups.title: Image And Status
stageGroups.encouragement: This round looks at how you present yourself.

questions.prompt: Before posting or sharing something, what do you check first?
questions.explanation: Sharing choices show whether honesty, response, or presentation leads.

questions.prompt: What makes you feel polished?
questions.explanation: Your version of polish reveals what you most want to project.

questions.prompt: When plans change suddenly, what bothers you most?
choices: You might not come across as well
questions.explanation: Sudden change shows whether you focus on others, your own steadiness, or how you come across.

questions.prompt: Which detail do you care about more than people realize?
questions.explanation: Small details reveal the part of the scene you naturally manage.

questions.prompt: What feels awkward to admit?
choices: You want to be seen as kind
You want to be taken seriously
questions.explanation: The wish that feels awkward often carries real emotional weight.

questions.prompt: If someone describes you inaccurately, what do you want to correct first?
questions.explanation: The first correction reveals which part of your identity feels most important.

stageGroups.title: Friendship And Romance
stageGroups.encouragement: Close connections show how easily attention can be shared.

questions.prompt: In a close connection, what do you appreciate most?
questions.explanation: Closeness can feel strongest through understanding, affirmation, or clarity.

questions.prompt: When someone close to you is excited, what do you do first?
choices: Give them room to enjoy it
questions.explanation: Shared excitement shows whether you join their feeling, connect it to yourself, or give them the moment.

questions.prompt: What makes you feel appreciated by people close to you?
questions.explanation: The appreciation you value most shows what you hope others notice.

questions.prompt: When plans with someone close change, what helps you reset?
questions.explanation: Resetting shows what kind of steadiness you need from others.

questions.prompt: What do you hope friends say about you when you are not there?
questions.explanation: The reputation you hope for points to the social role you like inhabiting.

questions.prompt: What is hardest when someone close needs the spotlight?
choices: Not adding your own moment too soon
questions.explanation: Other people's spotlight moments reveal how comfortably you share attention.

stageGroups.title: Boundaries And Accountability
stageGroups.encouragement: This round looks at boundaries, apologies, and shared attention.

questions.prompt: When someone says they need space, what is your first response?
choices: Respect it and check in later
Wonder if you did something wrong
questions.explanation: Space requests reveal how you balance care, uncertainty, and planning.

questions.prompt: What helps you apologize well?
choices: Knowing the right words to use
Having time to settle your feelings first
questions.explanation: Apology style shows whether empathy, wording, or emotional steadiness leads.

questions.prompt: When you realize you interrupted someone, what do you usually do?
choices: Pause and invite them back in
Try to make the interruption useful
questions.explanation: Interruptions show how quickly you can return space to someone else.

questions.prompt: What makes accountability easier?
choices: A chance to protect your dignity
questions.explanation: Accountability lands best when it fits the emotional conditions you trust.

questions.prompt: When a group decision does not go your way, what is most natural?
choices: Keep thinking your idea was stronger
questions.explanation: Group decisions show how easily you can release your preferred outcome.

questions.prompt: What does personal growth look like to you?
choices: Becoming more aware of shared space
questions.explanation: Your growth goal reveals the version of yourself you are quietly building.

stageGroups.title: Private Thoughts
stageGroups.encouragement: Private answers often reveal the clearest pattern.

questions.prompt: When do you feel most misunderstood?
choices: When people miss your good intentions
When people do not see your effort
questions.explanation: Feeling misunderstood often reveals what you most want recognized.

questions.prompt: Which thought visits you after a social event?
questions.explanation: After-the-fact thoughts show where your attention returns.

questions.prompt: What private wish feels most familiar?
choices: I want to be a better listener
I want people to notice my strengths
I want to feel less affected by comments
questions.explanation: Private wishes point toward the emotional skill you are practicing.

questions.prompt: What makes you feel quietly proud?
questions.explanation: Quiet pride reveals what your private standard rewards.

questions.prompt: What do you rarely say out loud?
choices: I care a lot about being kind
I care a lot about being admired
I care a lot about being right
questions.explanation: Unspoken priorities can be revealing without being dramatic.

questions.prompt: Which version of yourself do you protect most?
questions.explanation: The self you protect most often shapes your reaction patterns.

questions.prompt: Which description feels closest to you?
choices: I want confidence and kindness to stay balanced
I want to feel seen and appreciated
I want to look composed even when I am unsure
questions.explanation: The closest description points toward the pattern that feels most familiar.

questions.prompt: What do you want this result to understand about you?
choices: You are trying to be fair
You prefer knowing where things stand
questions.explanation: What you want understood can reveal the pattern underneath the answers.

questions.prompt: What feels like your biggest social lesson?
questions.explanation: Your lesson shows where your self-image is becoming more flexible.

questions.prompt: Which description feels most honest?
choices: One that shows your good intentions
questions.explanation: The most honest description reflects the part of yourself you notice most.

questions.prompt: What would make you feel more grounded?
choices: Being less attached to perfect presentation
questions.explanation: Feeling grounded often starts with calming the pattern that feels strongest.

questions.prompt: Which final answer feels most true today?
choices: I can be self-aware and still want recognition
I can enjoy attention without needing every moment
I can care about my image and still keep growing
questions.explanation: Your final choice closes the quiz with the pattern that feels strongest today.
